unchanged, will be checked on every member: the training members below (6x6, 7x7, 8x8) and LARGER members of the same

patrol) but other sizes, offsets and scattered obstacles. Rules that only work because of one member's exact
layout will fail there; describe the strategy so that it holds in every member.

## The world (the same in every member)
- An agent moves on an NxN grid: x = row (0 = top), y = column (0 = left). It starts at (0,0).
- Goals 1, 2, 3 must be visited in this order. Flag g1 becomes true when the agent enters goal 1's cell; g2 when it
  enters goal 2's cell while g1 is true; g3 when it enters goal 3's cell while g2 is true.
- Each step the agent picks up, right, down or left. The move succeeds with probability 0.7 and slips 90 degrees to
  either side with probability 0.15 each (e.g. `down` goes down 0.7, left 0.15, right 0.15).
- Moving off the grid or into a static obstacle leaves the agent where it is.
- A moving obstacle patrols a short path of cells, advancing one position per agent step through a cycle of 4
  positions (obs_idx 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 0 ...). Its cells may be entered, but being on the same cell as the
  obstacle at the same time is a collision.

## Requirements (checked exactly, in the WORST case)
- goal1, goal2, goal3: the agent eventually enters goal k's cell; probability >= 0.8 each.
- seq_1_before_2 / seq_2_before_3 / complete_sequence: goal 2's cell is never entered before goal 1, and goal 3's
  cell never before goals 1 and 2 (each, and both together); probability >= 0.8.
- avoid_moving_seg1/2/3: while heading to goal k, the agent never collides with the moving obstacle;
  probability >= 0.7 for each k.
"Worst case": wherever no rule applies, or a rule with action `any` allows several actions, an adversary picks
among the allowed actions to make the requirement fail. So every state must be covered, and every action a rule
allows must be safe. The adversary can also stall: if a rule allows a move that does not make progress (e.g. a
sideways or backwards move), the worst case may take it every time it can, and the agent may circle forever and
never reach the goal. Waiting is only safe when it ends: the obstacle's phase changes every step.

decides. Actions: up, right, down, left, or `any`. A rule with `any` allows every action for which its condition

The strategy is a priority cascade. Each rule uses only the sensors and flags, so it holds on any grid size.

1. **After all goals:** once g1, g2 and g3 are set, any action that avoids the obstacle is fine, since only entering goals matters from then on.
2. **Best progress:** prefer moves that are not walls, get closer to the next goal, avoid the patrol path, avoid entering a goal too early, avoid the obstacle's next cell, and are not risky (a slip cannot land on the patrol path or an early goal).
3. **Progress through the patrol:** the same progress moves, but allowed onto the patrol path when the obstacle is not arriving there. The `closer` sensor already routes around patrol cells unless no other route exists, so this covers corridors the patrol blocks.
4. **Plain progress:** any non-wall move that reduces the row or column difference to the next goal and is safe from early entry and the obstacle.
5. **Safe sideways moves:** if no progress move is available, any non-wall move that avoids the patrol path, early goals and the obstacle. The obstacle's phase changes every step, so this only delays.
6. **Wait:** if every move is blocked, a move into a wall keeps the agent in place, which is safe whenever the obstacle is not arriving there.
7. **Last resort:** any move that avoids early goals and the obstacle.
8. **Catch-all:** `true` with `any`, so no state is uncovered.

Every `any` rule only allows actions that its sensors have already checked, so the adversary can only choose among safe options. The one residual risk is stalling: if only sideways moves are safe, an adversary could alternate them, but the obstacle's phase keeps changing, so this does not persist.

  {"condition": "g1 & g2 & g3 & !obstacle", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "!wall & closer & !patrol & !early & !obstacle & !risky", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "!wall & closer & !patrol & !early & !obstacle", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "!wall & closer & !early & !obstacle", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "!wall & toward & !early & !obstacle", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "!wall & !patrol & !early & !obstacle", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "wall & !obstacle", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "!early & !obstacle", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "true", "action": "any"}
]}
```

## Strategy

1. **Progress first.** Take a move that goes towards the next unreached goal (`toward`) or along a shortest path (`closer`). Never enter a goal that must not be entered yet (`early`), and never hit a wall. Prefer moves that are also not `risky` and not on the patrol path.
2. **Patrol crossings are allowed only when the obstacle will not step onto the target next** (`!obstacle`). This is what lets the agent cross the patrol lane at the right phase. A patrol cell with `obstacle` false is entered safely at that phase, so the rules must not forbid patrol cells outright.
3. **Wait only when no progress move is safe.** A wall bump keeps the agent in place. Because waiting is allowed only when no progress move is allowed, the adversary cannot stall while progress is available. The patrol phase changes every step, so the obstacle clears and the progress move becomes allowed.
4. **Fallbacks last.** Non-progress safe moves, then any non-obstacle, non-early move, then a catch-all.

Since the first matching rule decides and `any` allows exactly the actions its condition holds for, each rule's condition restricts the allowed set. The early rules admit only safe progress. Waiting and detour rules come after, so they apply only when the earlier ones have no allowed action.

The rules use only sensors, flags and the obstacle phase, so they make no assumption about grid size, offsets or obstacle layout.

I have not verified the exact worst-case probabilities by simulating the MDP. The design removes the failing pattern (the `toward` move into a blocked patrol cell with no wait rule) and keeps slip-induced risks to single-step 0.15 exposures.

  {"condition": "g1 & g2 & g3 & !obstacle", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "!wall & toward & !patrol & !early & !obstacle & !risky", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "!wall & closer & !patrol & !early & !obstacle & !risky", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "!wall & (toward | closer) & !early & !obstacle", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "wall & !obstacle & !early & !risky", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "wall & !obstacle & !early", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "!wall & !patrol & !early & !obstacle & !risky", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "!wall & !early & !obstacle", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "!early & !obstacle", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "true", "action": "any"}
]}
```
